externalReview.identity: Full-time Dutch track Geschiedenis/GS, BA, 180 EC, Erasmus University Rotterdam, registry source row 20; not substituted with IB History.
externalReview.route: Economic History, option 1 minor/public role/internship, fixed by official order before UCR selection.
externalReview.formalRules: The adopted 2026–2027 Dutch ESHCC regulations control (article 10.3); Appendix 9 confirms the complete 180-EC History pathway. Preserve eight first-year courses (60 EC), three required second-year theory/method courses (22.5 EC), one complete 30-EC focus area, one 7.5-EC elective, 22.5 EC of thesis class/thesis and one 37.5-EC third-year option. Economic History and option 1 with internship remain the first-listed choices, independently of UCR fit. The elective and minor remain approved choice categories, without inventing subjects. Positive first-year study advice requires all 60 EC after permitted compensation (article 9.1); BA-2/3 exams require positive advice, subject to the article 4.3 personal-circumstances exception. The internship requires completed BA-1 and must be field-specific, normally in BA-3 term 2, completed within six consecutive months. Thesis-class entry requires completed BA-1 and at least 45 EC in BA-2/3 including three focus-area courses (22.5 EC); that class must be passed before submitting the thesis. The ordinary minor requires third-year registration and selection from the admission matrix. The 15-EC honours programme is extracurricular and excluded. Lectures are English, BA-1 practicals Dutch, later practicals Dutch/English; assessment may require English if the examiner does not master Dutch, and the GS thesis is written in Dutch. Marketing statements about all assessment being Dutch do not override article 3.3. The programme page uses a different philosophy-course code, but the formal title and 7.5 EC agree; no uncertain code is encoded.
externalReview.sourceResolution: The 2026–2027 Dutch OER controls over the English translation and undated marketing. Stored component titles/EC match Appendix 9. The public philosophy course code differs from the OER; no code is encoded and title/EC are unchanged. No material credit or curriculum-edition conflict was identified. Multiple direct PDF downloads and rendered PDF attempts timed out; current official indexed text was successfully inspected through the official Dutch/English media URLs. No PDF visual finding is claimed.
externalReview.choiceRestrictions: One complete 30-EC focus area; approved published elective and minor categories remain unspecified. Internship substitutes and exchange/educational routes are exclusive alternatives, not additional credits. Honours is outside 180.
externalReview.progression: 60-EC BA-1 after permitted compensation for positive study advice; positive advice before BA-2/3 exams with personal-circumstances exception. Internship after BA-1. Thesis class after BA-1 plus 45 BA-2/3 EC including three focus courses; class completion before thesis submission. Minor from third registration year and applicable admission matrix.
externalReview.nonCreditRequirements: Active participation and practical attendance required; BA-1 History has the special three-absence allowance, with missed assignments still due. Course guides control assessment/participation details. No extra EC invented.

academicReview.comparabilityChallenge: A coherent interdisciplinary programme and disclaimer alone do not establish a response to History. Here six direct History courses (45 EC) include chronology, thematic comparison and a primary-source research seminar. The closest is strengthened with three further historical/art-historiographic courses (22.5 EC), and all programmes have additional actual historical material, rather than relabelled generic courses. The degree’s defining study of historical change and evidence is sustained. Its fuller disciplinary sequence, Dutch scope and selected specialised focus, required thesis and placement remain explicit gaps. No degree-equivalence claim is made.
academicReview.closestCorrection: 21 of 24 closest courses preserved; two disproportionate adjacent courses and community rhetoric replaced with three actual historical/art-historiographic courses. Related schedules are preserved after actual content and concept review.
academicReview.candidateAndOwnership: All 17 generator rows assigned once; teaching candidate rejected for absent history pedagogy/secondary placement rather than absence of title alone. Eighteen support and seven search-only rows checked; no inherited or outcome-only basis promoted.

alignmentReview.reason: No single scheduled UCR course provides the external global survey from 1500 across Western and non-Western societies. Modern History is more strongly aligned to Global Societies, and the thematic History courses supply narrower studies.
Primary-source work is present in the advanced History Research Seminar, already aligned to the thesis class. There is no separately scheduled introductory historian-training course.

Both study early-modern cross-cultural encounters and the Renaissance. UCR focuses on Italian art and its Mediterranean/global connections through trade and colonisation, rather than the external course’s broader early-modern social history.
Past-present connections run through the programme, but no course directly delivers the external introductory historiography/relevance course.

Both substantively survey nineteenth- and twentieth-century political, economic and cultural change, including industrial societies, international power, crises and the welfare state. UCR begins in 1815 and extends to the present.
Both introduce sociological concepts and theories and their social-historical context. Erasmus explicitly applies them to historical research; UCR is a broader introductory sociology course.

Native American and gender histories offer substantial other historical studies, but none of the scheduled courses directly examines the Netherlands’ history and global position from the Middle Ages onward.
General rhetoric and PPD support academic writing, but do not require the external 4,000-word historical paper. The advanced primary-source seminar has a stronger relationship to the thesis class.
Both teach research design and quantitative/statistical analysis of empirical data. UCR provides general research/statistics training; Erasmus applies it specifically to historical data.

Both teach qualitative research design, interpretation and analysis of evidence. UCR undertakes general social-research projects; Erasmus specifically develops historical-source methods such as oral history, narrative and discourse analysis.
Art historiography is substantive but is not the external general philosophy-of-history course covering its central intellectual traditions.

Both substantively introduce international-relations theories and apply them through historical and contemporary cases. Erasmus specifically connects this field to economic globalisation since the nineteenth century; UCR’s scope is broader international relations.
No scheduled UCR course directly studies historical relationships between multinationals and nation-states. General organisational psychology has been withdrawn and is not an adequate counterpart.
Introductory economics supplies analytical context but does not teach the external historical cases of emerging economies and global labour. Keep this component separate.

Both directly examine economic inequality and the relation of institutions/policy to distribution. UCR focuses on economic models and evidence about taxation, spending and redistribution; Erasmus investigates capitalism and inequality historically.
The approved 7.5-EC elective subject remains unspecified; no single UCR course is asserted as its counterpart.

Both involve advanced historical primary-source inquiry and a substantial research paper. UCR researches the 1809 Walcheren Expedition; Erasmus prepares a separate Economic History thesis. The UCR seminar does not deliver that focus-area thesis.
The external 15-EC individual thesis is compulsory. No scheduled UCR course is a bachelor thesis; optional independent research is displayed alongside it outside the UCR 180 EC.
The approved 15-EC minor is a choice category, not one scheduled UCR course.
PPD and primary-school rhetoric are complementary skills/community engagement, not a course on historians’ professional and societal practice.
The selected 15-EC field-specific internship is not delivered by any scheduled UCR course.
